boxes.label: Theorem C35
boxes.statement: Any finite triangle-free simple graph with no independent set of size 10 that contains an induced copy of the circulant C35(1,7,11,16) (vertices 0..34, u ~ v iff v − u ≡ ±1, ±7, ±11 or ±16 mod 35) has at most 39 vertices, and any four distinct vertices outside the copy induce a 4-cycle.
boxes.also: So no triangle-free graph on 40 vertices with no independent 10-set contains an induced C35(1,7,11,16).
boxes.posed: The question was posed in public before: by Unsolved Lab (M20, 1 Oct, not run), in the repository andrey-kokoev/marici (a note dated 9 Nov: “this extension family has not been excluded”) and by an idea scout of Chen’s run (21 Nov, timed out). Nobody had decided it.

corollary.text: In a triangle-free graph on 40 vertices with no independent set of size 10, deleting any 5 vertices leaves an independent set of size 9; so at least 6 deletions are needed to leave none.
corollary.label: prose proof, not in Lean, conditional on Goedgebeur–Radziszowski’s uniqueness of the (3,9;35)-graph

boxes.why39: Call the copy’s 35 vertices the core and the rest outside. If an outside vertex were unjoined to two other outside vertices, their three core-neighbourhoods would be three sets that Lemma P, a finite fact checked by computer, says cannot exist; so the missing edges among the outside vertices form a matching. Five outside vertices missing only a matching always contain a triangle, so there are at most four, and 35 + 4 = 39; four with no triangle must miss two disjoint edges, which leaves exactly a 4-cycle.

exoo_square.text: Of the 82,251 ways to remove four of the 39 vertices of Exoo’s 1989 graph, exactly one leaves an induced copy of C35(1,7,11,16), and the four removed vertices induce a 4-cycle: the equality case of the theorem appears in Exoo’s example.
exoo_square.caveat: checked on the isomorphism class identified from our own files; Exoo’s pinned bytes were not at home

boxes.smaller_certificate: A smaller certificate for Lemma P: 385 of the 3,360 independent 8-sets suffice, in five orbits of the circulant’s 210 affine symmetries (105 + 70 + 70 + 105 + 35). No union of whole orbits with fewer sets works (1,082 non-empty unions checked). Smaller sub-families exist (an irredundant one of 368 sets), so 385 is minimal only among unions of whole orbits. Confirmed by our own search and by a SAT proof that lrat-check and cake_lpr accept.
boxes.found_by: The square and the smaller certificate were found in a reading by GPT-6.2-astra (via Carlos Toledo’s chat) and checked by our own code.

boxes.label: Case R(7), a second computation
boxes.statement: If P1–P6 hold (as they stand in item 1 above): no 9-regular triangle-free graph on 40 vertices with independence number at most 9 has two non-adjacent vertices with exactly 7 common neighbours.
boxes.set_equal: Our 977,008 configurations are Chen’s package pairs, set for set, by our reading of his pair_packages.py: his filters re-implemented, not run.
boxes.adds: What ours adds to C-004, as facts: LRAT proofs; two checkers, one formally verified (cake_lpr); a Lean proof that the encoding is sound (T0, T1); the CNF bytes recomputed from the Lean definition on every row (T2, computed); the premises written out; the rules timestamped before the pod existed; four controls before production.
